newsitem.title: USA: Florida death row attorneys seek to halt executions.
newsitem.headline: Florida death row attorneys seek to halt executions.

text.p: The Florida Supreme Court said on Tuesday it will hear arguments next month from state-funded attorneys who say Florida must halt executions because they can no longer afford to defend death row inmates.

The court's clerk set an emergency hearing for May 13 after the office of Capital Collateral Representatives (CCR), which defends prisoners facing execution, said it was bankrupt and asked that death row proceedings be halted until the agency was given more money to do its job.
Michael Minerva, the agency's chief, had resigned on Friday and filed an emergency petition saying that an explosion of death row appeals had exhausted the agency's resources.

"CCR is presently out of money," he wrote. "To keep up with what has been demanded of CCR has cost CCR significantly more to operate during this fiscal year... than it did for the entire fiscal year of 1995-96."

Lawmakers said the filing was an effort by CCR staff members to halt executions. "It's a ploy to stop executions," Al Gutman, chairman of the Senate Criminal Justice Committee, told the St. Petersburg Times. "They'll do anything including mismanaging their own budget, to stop executions."
Minerva had been complaining of staff cuts and a burgeoning caseload for months.

Minerva blamed the situation on lawmakers, who cut funding for the programme at the same time that new rules were enacted that indefinitely extend death warrants. The combination of those factors has resulted in a huge increase in appellate activity that CCR is unable to undertake, he said.

The filing came as death penalty advocates and opponents debate the constitutionality of the use of Florida's electric chair. A mishap last month sent flames shooting from an inmate's head during his execution, prompting the state Supreme Court to stay further executions until the issue has been decided.
